example.scenario: Adversaries compromise a widely used open-source JavaScript library's NPM package by injecting malicious code into a dependency update, which is then distributed to thousands of downstream projects via automatic dependency updates.

indicators: Presence of event-stream@3.3.6 as a new dependency in malicious-lib@2.3.1
Outbound TCP connection from developer build machines to malicious.attacker.com on port 6667
Unusual file system read attempts for ~/.ssh/id_rsa in application logs
Git commit metadata authored by unknown or suspicious users
Network traffic showing encrypted data to unknown external IPs during build process
NPM package published from unusual IP address without prior history
example.detection_method: Monitor package dependency changes via SBOM tooling; alert on unexpected new dependencies especially with native modules or network access; enforce strict code signing and verify signatures on dependencies; network monitoring for unusual outbound connections during build and runtime; audit git commit logs and verify commit authors; integrate vulnerability scanning and alert on known vulnerable or suspicious packages; implement runtime behavioral analytics to detect unauthorized file accesses and network connections.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1195.002 - Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
T1059.004 - Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
